label: RW Aurigae
position_source: SIMBAD (simbad.harvard.edu) V* RW Aur, moved to 2026.0

scale.method: linear, 1.0-99.5 percentile of good pixels of all frames (same scale for every frame)

method: up to 8 exposures per visit (closest to the visit's mean time), each IMAGE - ZODI with the official flag mask, reprojected onto this grid and added up with 1/variance weights
notes: Each add-up mixes exposures at different wavelengths (at the star 1.18–1.39, 1.12–1.65 and 1.11–1.64 µm), so the frames alone cannot say how much RW Aurigae changed; the light curve below compares single exposures at matching wavelengths instead.

At matching wavelengths (1.2-1.27 µm) it was fainter in Sep 2025 than in Sep 2026: 24% in the one pair with no flagged pixels, 24-83% in the 4 pairs that include flagged pixels. Mar and Sep 2026 agree (ratios 0.89-1.03 at 1.11 and 1.6 µm). A star in the Barnard field, measured the same way, changes by about 5%.
The Sep 2025 exposures also differ by 10-20% from each other within 2 hours; whether the star or the measurement causes this is not checked.
Gaia DR3 lists a second star 1.5″ away (G 12.18; RW Aurigae is a known double star). Both are inside the measuring circle.
Gaia says RW Aurigae moves 0.004 pixels over the year, yet the difference view shows a small bright-dark pair at the star: that is the size of pair that alignment and PSF differences alone make.
